rounds.text: Vivo Collaboration Solutions Ltd is currently undergoing a significant operational turnaround that the market has yet to fully price in. While the company struggled with long-term sales contraction [E13, E14, E48], the most recent data confirms a powerful inflection point with trailing twelve-month sales growth of 25% [E15] and year-over-year sales growth reaching 45% [E52]. This momentum is supported by a broader sector tailwind where the median sales growth is 19.4% [E60], and the company is successfully capitalizing on this environment with profit growth exceeding 1-year price growth by 17% [E44]. The stock remains fundamentally inexpensive, trading at a price-to-book ratio of 1.36x [E1], which is a deep discount compared to the sector benchmark of 7.35x [E6]. Furthermore, the company is demonstrating superior capital efficiency relative to its peers, maintaining an ROA of -7.48% against a significantly worse sector benchmark of -40.72% [E7]. Conceded: [E3, E8, E13, E14, E48].

Vivo Collaboration Solutions Ltd presents a concerning long-term trajectory characterized by persistent revenue erosion, as evidenced by compounded sales growth of -26% over five years and -24% over three years [E13, E14, E48]. This structural decline is further underscored by a negative return on equity of -8.06%, which significantly underperforms the sector benchmark of 10.06% [E8]. Investors are currently receiving no compensation for these risks, as the company offers a dividend yield of 0.00% [E3]. While the company shows a recent uptick in sales growth, this must be weighed against the historical inability to sustain top-line expansion [E13, E14, E15, E52]. Conceded: [E1, E6, E7, E15, E44, E52, E53, E55, E60]. The reliance on a recent, short-term performance shift to justify a market capitalization of ₹ 15.6 Cr ignores the deeper, multi-year trend of value destruction [E2, E13, E14].
